start_date.summary: The article explicitly dates the action to 13 February 2021.

end_date.summary: No physical end time or termination is reported; the end date remains unknown.

location.summary: The article places the assembly at the Shaheed Minar premises in Dhaka.

organizer.summary: The article identifies citizens including teachers and activists; it does not name a formal convening organization.

demands.summary: Participants demanded government repeal of the Digital Security Act and immediate, unconditional release of two people detained under it.

participants.summary: The report says over 250 people joined; no maximum or exact count is supplied.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported lower-bound phrase “over 250” exceeds the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not describe violence by participants; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The article does not describe state action in response to this assembly; all seven response variables remain unknown.

scope.summary: One Dhaka gathering is described; no other location is combined.

episode_key.summary: Tentative single-day assembly key. No uninterrupted occupation or evidence linking this rally to separate February 27 or March 1 events is established.

notes: One February 13 Dhaka assembly is documented by one contemporary report, with a reported lower-bound crowd of over 250 and direct government-law demands. Event end and state response are not described. It remains a distinct candidate from later DSA-related demonstrations because shared grievance does not establish one uninterrupted episode.
open_questions: Coordinator review of demand category and provisional eligibility.
Physical end time and state response are not reported.

title: BNP rally in Dhaka against proposed revocation of Ziaur Rahman’s gallantry title
location: In front of the National Press Club, Dhaka
organizer: Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and front organizations
participants_original: Hundreds of BNP and front-organization supporters from across the country, according to Dhaka Tribune
threshold_50_evidence: The contemporary report describes hundreds of party and front-organization supporters joining the Dhaka rally; no exact count is given.

occurrence.summary: Dhaka Tribune reports the BNP rally and ensuing police intervention in front of the National Press Club on 13 February.

start_date.summary: The article identifies Saturday 13 February 2021 and says the rally began around 10:00.

end_date.summary: Police foiled the rally and began clearing the street around noon, but the article does not establish a physical end; end remains unknown.

location.summary: The report locates the local assembly in front of the National Press Club in Dhaka.

organizer.summary: The article identifies BNP and its front organizations as organizers/participants.

demands.summary: The party opposed the government decision to revoke founder Ziaur Rahman’s Bir Uttam gallantry title.

participants.summary: The report says hundreds attended; no precise count is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The body’s plural “hundreds” clearly exceeds 50, though it is not a precise count.

protester_violence.summary: The article reports BNP activists hurled brickbats and stones at police during the clashes.

state_response.summary: Police baton-charged demonstrators and cleared the street; police said at least 18 people were held. Other state-response variables remain unknown.

scope.summary: Dhaka is coded as a single local assembly. The report mentions separate metropolitan rallies under the same program, but does not combine their participants or locations.

episode_key.summary: Tentative one-day Dhaka event; this item is kept separate from other party-led demonstrations because date/location and grievance differ.

notes: One local Dhaka rally under a wider BNP program; no nationwide attendance is inferred. The party’s affiliation alone does not establish the manual’s narrow multi-party/election exclusion. The article documents an issue with a government decision about state honors. End time unknown despite police foiling the event; participant injuries/detentions are not used as attendance.
open_questions: Coordinator review of demand category and provisional eligibility.
Physical end time not stated; do not treat publication time or the first police intervention as the event end.

title: Freedom-fighters’ offspring stage Shahbagh sit-in for government-service quota
location: Shahbagh intersection and National Museum area, Dhaka
organizer: Bangladesh Muktijoddha Santan Sangsad (also reported as Bangladesh Muktijoddha Sontan)
participants_original: Hundreds of protesters, according to bdnews24.com
threshold_50_evidence: The contemporary bdnews24.com body describes hundreds of protesters taking position at the Shahbagh intersection; the exact count is not reported.

occurrence.summary: Two contemporary reports describe the 23 February sit-in/blockade at Shahbagh organized by a freedom-fighters’ offspring group.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the gathering to 23 February. The Daily Star gives a 10:00 National Museum gathering and noon move to Shahbagh; bdnews24 places gathering at the intersection around 11:00. Exact starting time/location sequence remains imprecise.

end_date.summary: bdnews24 reports police chased the protesters away with water cannons around 18:00 on 23 February.

location.summary: The sit-in blocked Shahbagh intersection in Dhaka; one report also places the initial assembly near the National Museum.

organizer.summary: The reports name Bangladesh Muktijoddha Sontan and Bangladesh Muktijoddha Santan Sangsad, respectively; exact organizational naming/linkage remains a review point.

demands.summary: Both report a seven-point claim including a 30 percent quota in government jobs/services for freedom-fighters’ offspring.

participants.summary: One report describes hundreds arriving from around Bangladesh; exact number and count method are unknown.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The body explicitly says hundreds took position at the intersection, above the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The reports do not establish protester violence; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Police used water cannons and chased protesters away. The organizer alleged detentions and injuries; police denied these, so arrests remain unknown. Other response fields remain unknown.

scope.summary: A single Shahbagh sit-in in Dhaka is reported; no other location is merged.

episode_key.summary: Tentative one-day event key from matching date, Shahbagh location, organizer group and seven-point quota claim; it does not authorize merging a broader quota campaign.

notes: Both reports describe one Shahbagh assembly, but give different approximate early chronology: Daily Star reports an approximately 10:00 gathering by the National Museum and move around noon; bdnews24 says protesters gathered at Shahbagh around 11:00. The date, place and quota claim align. bdnews24 says hundreds and reports dispersal around 18:00. The Daily Star page gives no attendance or physical ending. No exact attendance count is inferred.
open_questions: Confirm the precise organizer naming or relationship between the two reports without inferring syndication.
Exact participant count and any state responses beyond reported dispersal remain unknown.
Coordinator should review the provisional demand taxonomy and event eligibility.

title: JCD rally in Dhaka against DSA and Mushtaq Ahmed’s custodial death
location: National Press Club precinct and adjacent road, Dhaka
organizer: Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), the student wing of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)
participants_original: JCD leader said around 500 had gathered inside the press club; police said 400–500 activists tried to take position on the road. Estimates retained separately, not summed or averaged.
threshold_50_evidence: Both source-attributed descriptions put the assembly above 50: the JCD leader said around 500 were gathered inside, and police described 400–500 activists trying to enter the road.

occurrence.summary: Prothom Alo reports the JCD/BNP gathering and police clash outside the National Press Club on 28 February.

start_date.summary: The article identifies 28 February 2021 and says members began gathering around 10:00am.

end_date.summary: Police chased and dispersed participants, but a BNP/JCD group later occupied the BMA corner and the article does not establish that the full gathering ended.

location.summary: The report locates the rally at the National Press Club and the adjacent road/BMA building area in Dhaka.

organizer.summary: The source identifies Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal as organizer and BNP as the parent/opposition party.

demands.summary: JCD leaders described demands concerning Mushtaq Ahmed’s death in custody, DSA repeal, and the planned revocation of Ziaur Rahman’s gallantry award.

participants.summary: JCD leader said around 500 gathered inside the Press Club; police estimated 400–500 trying to take position on the road. Different estimates/sites are preserved without reconciliation.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Each reported estimate exceeds 50; no injuries or detentions are used as attendance.

protester_violence.summary: The report says BNP/JCD participants threw brickbats at police and vandalised the area.

state_response.summary: Police baton-charged and beat participants and used empty and tear-gas shells to disperse; police also said several were taken into custody. Exact detention count is not stated.

scope.summary: One Dhaka assembly is coded locally. No attendance from other cities or separate BNP events is combined.

episode_key.summary: Tentative single-day Dhaka event; separate from earlier 13 February BNP rally and 26–27 February student-group demonstrations. Shared party membership or grievance does not establish uninterrupted physical occupation.

notes: Provisional include: a documented single-party student-wing rally, with demands concerning DSA repeal and custody accountability, meets the reported size threshold. Political affiliation alone is not treated as an exclusion; the reported action is not an election protest or multi-party election coalition. Source reports both rally and police force, but does not prove physical end time or detention number. Mushtaq died in custody before this protest.
open_questions: Coordinator review of provisional eligibility and demand category.
Exact end time, exact crowd count and number detained are unknown.
The reported empty shells are not evidence that live ammunition was fired.

demands.summary: Students demanded reopening of the university campus and residential halls; whether this targets national government policy or university administration remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is reported; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No state response is described; all response dimensions remain unknown.

notes: Provisional lead. The approximate attendance may straddle the 50-person cutoff, and the article does not clarify whether the demanded reopening decision is addressed to national government or university administration. Do not combine with the separately mentioned SUST action.

Physical end and state response are unreported.

title: Nurses and midwives rally over professional equivalence and licensing policy
location: In front of the National Museum, Shahbagh, Dhaka
organizer: S009 names Bangladesh Student Nurses and Midwives Combined Council; S050 does not name a convenor.
participants_original: Neither contemporary report gives an attendance count. S009 describes registered nurses and midwives rallying in the afternoon; S050 describes unemployed diploma nurses assembled in the morning.
threshold_50_evidence: The two reports provide no attendance number; at least 50 simultaneous participants is not established.

occurrence.summary: Two reports describe nursing-profession demonstrations outside the National Museum at Shahbagh on 13 February over equivalency and licensing policy; they may describe one or two assemblies.

start_date.summary: Both reports identify 13 February; one places the rally in the afternoon and the other in the morning.

end_date.summary: Neither report gives a physical termination time.

location.summary: Both reports place the action in front of the National Museum at Shahbagh, Dhaka.

organizer.summary: S009 identifies the Bangladesh Student Nurses and Midwives Combined Council; S050 describes unemployed diploma nurses without naming a convenor.

demands.summary: The reports describe opposition to diploma equivalence and demands concerning professional licensing/examinations; S009 says speakers appealed to the prime minister and health minister.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance count establishes the 50-person cutoff.

protester_violence.summary: Neither article reports protester violence; state is retained as unknown.

state_response.summary: Neither article reports a government or police response to the assembly.

scope.summary: Both actions are reported at one local Dhaka site.

episode_key.summary: Shared date/site and overlapping professional demands suggest a possible relationship, but differing time and participant descriptions leave one-versus-two assembly ownership unresolved.

open_questions: Do S009 and S050 describe one rally or separate morning and afternoon assemblies?
Did either assembly reach at least 50 simultaneous participants?
What was the physical end time and was there any response to the demands?

end_date.summary: Students lifted the blockade after a university-administration promise to seek arrests; the report does not give an exact time.

title: Barishal University students renew highway blockade after police arrest transport workers
location: Barishal-Kuakata highway near the University of Barishal main gate, Barishal
organizer: University of Barishal students; no named organizing body reported.
participants_original: Multiple reports describe the blockade; none gives a protester count. A source’s “over 50 students” refers to people allegedly dispossessed of phones, not assembly attendance.
threshold_50_evidence: No source gives an attendance count. Counts of affected students, injured students or travellers are not crowd-size evidence.

occurrence.summary: Contemporary reports describe students blocking a Barishal highway on 20 February after police arrested two transport workers in the conflict over attacks on students.

start_date.summary: Reports place the student sit-in/blockade at about 09:30 on 20 February.

end_date.summary: Students withdrew around 18:00 and postponed further agitation; exact physical ending is approximate.

location.summary: The blockade was on the Barishal-Kuakata highway near the University of Barishal main gate.

organizer.summary: Reports identify University of Barishal students; no formal organizing organization is named.

demands.summary: Students sought arrests and a criminal case over the dormitory attack, safety, and return of phones; whether the action was directed to state authorities or other parties needs review.

participants.summary: No protest turnout is reported. “Over 50 students” describes people whose phones or wallets were allegedly taken, not assembly attendees.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No assembly headcount is reported; counts of affected students or travellers cannot establish the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: Reports describe attacks attributed to transport workers and arrests by police; none establishes violence by protesters.

state_response.summary: Police and university statements/actions are reported in the broader conflict, but no protest-response value is assigned without clearer attribution to this action.

scope.summary: The student blockade is a local Barishal action.

episode_key.summary: The reports describe separate blockades on 17 and 20 February within the same dispute; the original episode rule leaves their relationship open.

open_questions: Was the demand directed to a domestic public authority, and which one?
Did the student assembly reach at least 50 people?
Does this renewed blockade count as a separate event from 17 February under the source rules?
What was the exact physical endpoint and what state response was directed at this blockade?
notes: Separate from the transport-workers’ action at Rupatali. Do not use affected students or commuters as attendance.

location.summary: The action was at Rupatali bus terminal/Chaumatha in Barishal.

organizer.summary: The report attributes the action to Rupatali Bus Sramik Union members.
